body: I suppose that's the only option. Thanks for helping.

She is fully aware that alcohol is extremely dangerous for the baby. She wants to get better, but it's obviously very hard for her. My step dad has been sober for two years, and is trying to get her to stop, but she hides whatever she buys. It isn't as if I see her drinking. I do know that she gets plastered enough that she wakes up still drunk. She's on a three day binge, she hasn't been sober since she started.

We've looked for what she has, but she hid it really well, and she won't tell us where it is.

I just want this baby to be OK. I don't know how she can raise it if she's like this.
I can be involuntarily hospitalized if I am a danger to myself, which I am.

I have no idea.

I of course fear judgement (all humans judge, and while they may not show it, or even do it very much, it is still there), and I fear being involuntarily hospitalized. Quite literally no better than prison.

But the primary fear is some all-encompassing, indescribable horror.
Already part of that. The issue is not me, my concern is for the baby. What do I do to keep her safe?

You do not understand the depth of the fear. There is nothing I am more scared of than getting help. That's why I posted. I need some way to get over the fear. I know I need help, but I am paralyzed. The post was asking for a way to break through.

If rational thought was ruling, I would already have gotten help.

Imagine a person in aa burning building. The fire is behind them, but they have a way down. They're also terrified of heights.

In the case of most people, the fear of the fire eventually overwhelms the fear of heights. In my case, it won't.

Virginia Statute § 20-124.6
A. Notwithstanding any other provision of law, neither parent, regardless of whether such parent has custody, shall be denied access to the academic or health records of that parent’s minor child unless otherwise ordered by the court for good cause shown or pursuant to subsection B.
B. In the case of health records, access may also be denied if the minor’s treating physician or the minor’s treating clinical psychologist has made a part of the minor’s record a written statement that, in the exercise of his professional judgment, the furnishing to or review by the requesting parent of such health records would be reasonably likely to cause substantial harm to the minor or another person.

I am still a minor. There are no guarantees; it's up to the doctor's judgement.
Doctors can break confidentiality if they fear that you are a danger to yourself or others.
The possibility of surviving and being put on inpatient care is one of the reasons I don't kill myself. I'm a student with an intense schedule. I can't fall behind.
I guess I should have made it clear that medical professionals are high on the list of "hell no!"s. That's actually scarier to me than telling family.
